<STRUCT_0001>
Given a scheme <MATH_0001> and an action of a group <MATH_0002> on <MATH_0003> we say the action
of <MATH_0004> on <MATH_0005> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>free<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if condition <MATH_0006> of Lemma <REF_0001>
holds. This is equivalent to the notion of a free action of the constant
group scheme <MATH_0007> on <MATH_0008> as defined in
Groupoids, Definition <REF_0002>.
The lemma can be interpreted as saying that quotients of schemes by
free actions of groups exist in the category of algebraic spaces.

Notation <MATH_0001>, <MATH_0002>, <MATH_0003> as in Lemma <REF_0001>.
If the action of <MATH_0004> on <MATH_0005> satisfies <MATH_0006> we say <MATH_0007> <TEXTITOPEN_0001>acts freely<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
on the scheme <MATH_0008>. In this case the algebraic space <MATH_0009> is denoted
<MATH_0010> and is called the <TEXTITOPEN_0002>quotient of <MATH_0011> by <MATH_0012><TEXTITCLOSE_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001>
This notation is consistent with the notation <MATH_0001> introduced in
Groupoids, Definition <REF_0001>.
We will later make sense of the quotient as an algebraic stack without
any assumptions on the action whatsoever; when we do this we will use the
notation <MATH_0002>. Before we discuss the examples we prove
some more lemmas to facilitate the discussion. Here is a lemma discussing the
various separation conditions for this quotient when <MATH_0003> is finite.
